props.heading:
Promises, not
statistics.
Before you get in touch
props.body: The things people usually ask first.

items.q: Do I need an app, or just a website?
items.a: Most businesses need a website first, and we will say so rather than sell you an app. An app earns its keep when customers come back again and again: booking, ordering, loyalty, or staff who need something on their phone.

items.q: Do you deal with Apple and Google for us?
items.a: Yes. We set up the store listings, write the privacy declarations, submit the builds and answer the reviewers. We have taken our own apps through Apple review and Google Play, so we know where they get held up.

items.q: Can we try the app before it goes live?
items.a: Yes. You get test builds on your own phone through Apple TestFlight and Google Play testing, and nothing goes to the public stores until you have signed it off.

items.q: How long does a website take?
items.a: Seven days for our website packages. Apps, staff portals and larger integrations vary too much to put a number on here, so we agree a date at scoping and stick to it.

items.q: Can you connect it to what we already use?
items.a: Usually, yes. We have built against Microsoft 365, Stripe, Supabase, Twilio, Resend and Apple and Google push notifications. Tell us what you run and we will say plainly whether it is straightforward or will add cost.

items.q: Do we own the app or website afterwards?
items.a: Yes. You get the source code and design files, the domain stays in your name, and the apps can sit under your own developer accounts. Nothing is rented to you.

props.eyebrow: Got an app or a site in mind?
props.heading: Tell us what it needs to do.
